approach.method_basis: The Parent grows a tree of molecular graph edits and buys each new frontier molecule directly. Every accepted score updates only the occurrence path that generated it. Selection shares receipt-backed peak returns, completed visits and pending visits among chemically similar siblings. After a strict incumbent improvement it starts a fresh episode with two ordered origins, the new incumbent and the incumbent from before that feedback boundary, each initialized from its own original accepted receipt. The supplied initial forest, direct-frontier purchases and exact route accounting remain part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: At promoted roots, remove only the completed visits borrowed from the other origin when calculating exploration and zero-start priority. Each origin will use its own completed count together with the existing shared pending count, while the existing shared peak value remains active. This tests whether sharing completed exploration counts suppresses useful root allocation. Earlier siblings removed both exploration densities together, removed shared peak values, or removed one density under own peak values; none measured this single completed-count consumer with shared values retained.

observed_bottleneck: The dual-origin Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 obtains real access to both origins but does not convert that access into better paid search: all 115 preceding origins obtain descendants and 1,686 paid descendants come from them, yet the complete mean is 0.4809700595412967 (SD 0.025313161830483537), down 0.018526255130948004 from its code Parent n-e4b751133c75. Full/late incumbent-increment mass is 4.087169227484811/4,350 and 0.8656010443094923/2,175, with late rate down 0.00023074116049972773. All fifteen Search cells completed with valid unique purchases. Thus membership benefit was refuted, while actual-return bookkeeping and both-origin access remain implemented capabilities. The specific unresolved bottleneck is statistical root allocation: D includes completed returns borrowed from the other origin, which suppresses the exploration bonus without representing extra actual visits to this origin. n-8d598efc7e40 jointly removes completed and pending borrowing with shared values and gains only 0.002089580176201663; n-fc3b91c9623a removes shared peak values and n-51af92d7316d removes values and both densities. Single completed/pending removals n-bf023e9ce9f8 and n-0fdf8aec31a2 lose 0.006156349369649307 and 0.04013074283123318 under own values, a different composition. These results do not determine the isolated completed/shared-value sign. Source-pinned original-state replay independently checked in policy/scratch/r0060-00-improve-L01/plan-evidence.json reproduces 581 changed choices of 3,715 promoted-root decisions, joined to 549 actual paid paths, 295 late; all 7,430 rows have borrowed completed density. This is exposure evidence only, not alternative reward evidence.

hypothesis: Remove only the off-diagonal completed-count term from the exploration and zero-start-priority consumer when episode > 0 and parent_id == 0. For each currently eligible origin i, retain the inherited kernel records D_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij*O_j, B_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j*M_j, and shared exploitation B_i/D_i (or its inherited neutral default). Replace started_i=D_i+P_i by started_i=N_i+P_i solely for active exploration and the started_i==0 priority. Keep beta=0.5, the parent N+O logarithmic numerator and earliest-occurrence ties. Because K_ii=1 and off-diagonal K_ij*N_j is nonnegative, removing it decreases started on exposed rows and weakly increases their bonus without changing shared value or shared pending support. Different bonuses can change which accepted origin supplies a direct frontier purchase. Only the complete paid panel can determine this consumer's conditional retained contribution; joint-density effects and own-value signs are not assumed to transfer.

finding_summary.headline: Completed-count removal changed paid search, but lost 0.01274 mean score and failed its preservation prediction.
finding_summary.insights:
Execution and changed allocation are established; the prediction that this removal would preserve scores is refuted. Under the retained shared-value/shared-pending composition, the completed-count consumer has positive conditional retained contribution. The three-seed variation makes that a descriptive result for this frozen panel, not a significance claim or a universal advantage. The late improvement does not rescue the endpoint claim, and it is not evidence that changed-choice descendants mediated that improvement: only two of the 699 changed-route purchases improved the incumbent, and none of the 472 late changed-route purchases did. Those adaptive strata have no measured alternative rewards. The membership intervention remains refuted, and this result neither assigns separate identities to the count consumers nor determines their interactions or the fate of the broader tree approach. No RAVE estimator or blending method was introduced or tested.

The method still reaches both incumbent origins but tends toward local refinement: fragment-excluded within-session similarity rises from 0.40124 across the full window to 0.46373 late, while pooled typed/generic scaffold counts fall to 1,755/1,240 from the Parent’s 1,837/1,284. This is not total scaffold collapse. Both size tails persist and enlarge: 341 molecules below six heavy atoms and 250 above fifty, versus 319 and 244; late counts are 184/152 versus 170/141. Molecular assessment associates the weak docking seed with a different nitrogen environment and shows that useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements are reachable but inconsistently preserved, alongside questionable heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. That supports a limitation in the graph proposal operator’s preservation of useful local chemistry, without establishing the cause of a particular score loss. A proposal operator that makes coherent fragment or scaffold changes while preserving attachment context is the kind of method that could address this limitation; its benefit remains untested. The current evidence does not diagnose surrogate ranking error because this direct-frontier method has no learned surrogate ranking stage.
finding_summary.results:
All fifteen Search sessions completed. Exploration bonuses increased on all 7,528 exposed promoted-root rows, while shared peak values, shared pending counts and all 33,816 rows outside that gate stayed exact at the same state. There were 737 changed root choices among 3,764 promoted-root decisions: 699 reached paid molecules and 38 ended in failed routes. Changed routes covered 699 of 4,350 full purchases and 472 of 2,175 late purchases. Three task/seed cells had no changed paid choices, including the session with no root promotion; they remain in every denominator. Receipt, pending-count, widening, root-context and backup checks found no isolation mismatch.

Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 4.08717 to 3.89612, with 146 strict improvements versus 148. Late gain mass rose from 0.86560 to 1.03907, with 46 strict improvements on each side. Mean final Top-1 nevertheless fell from 0.480970 to 0.468234, a paired change of −0.012736. The three seed changes were +0.014003, −0.072016 and +0.019804; eight endpoints improved, four declined and three tied. The largest endpoint loss was 0.448131 on the second docking seed. The complete mean loss exceeds the registered descriptive 0.002 scale, triggering the score-preserving-removal falsifier. The result remains 0.138797 below the formal Anchor, whose unchanged improvement target was not reached.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and polycyclic output retains fragments, oversized recombinations, unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Complete Child evaluation and complete code-Parent pairing are separately true in context.comparison. All fifteen Search task/seed trajectories were read for n-038a8161afbb and the published n-b13ef5ae4ba8; no task or Parent path is missing. Each side contains 4500 accepted records including 150 initial records, with 4350 optimizer purchases. Initial records are excluded from all generated-chemistry counts. The late window is optimizer ordinals 146–290, 2175 purchases, including the crossing announcement's final five. The bounded digest's final_molecules excerpt is not an all-seed endpoint summary; full trajectories were used. No held-out or Confirmation evidence was read. The Child output spans 1–107 heavy atoms (median 26), with 3902/4350 ring-containing and 3401/4350 aromatic molecules. Its digest ring-closure rates range from 0.8517 to 0.9184 and aromatic-marker rates from 0.5322 to 0.8851, consistent with abundant rings and aromatic chemistry. Parent spans 1–117 heavy atoms (median 26), with 3918 ring-containing and 3373 aromatic molecules. This is a broad formal graph vocabulary: aromatic amides and ethers, fused heteroaromatics/diones, cyclic amines, polycyclic acetals/cages and small cleavage products. Ordinary medicinal motifs coexist with N/O halogenation, peroxides, N–O/N–N linkages, crowded topologies and missing stereochemistry. The quality labels describe these structures; neither scores nor canonical validity establish synthesis, stability, potency or suitable exposure. Child full <6/>50-heavy-atom tails are 341/250 of 4350, and late tails 184/152 of 2175; Parent is 319/244 and 170/141. Child nonempty pooled typed/generic Murcko counts are 1755/1240 full and 991/730 late, with 448/215 empty scaffolds. Parent is 1837/1284 and 1042/776, with 432/211 empty scaffolds. These pooled unique counts differ from sums of per-cell distinct counts, which are preserved in the audits. Similarity is independently recomputed using radius-two chiral sparse-count Morgan generalized dot-product Tanimoto, dot(x,y)/(dot(x,x)+dot(y,y)-dot(x,y)), over all unordered pairs within each task/seed/window after excluding molecules below six heavy atoms. Pair-weighted Child means are 0.4012424740824044/0.4637296114058281 full/late over 534091/131383 pairs from 4009/1991 molecules; Parent means are 0.408657415704561/0.46865056710571285 over 540155/133298 pairs from 4031/2005 molecules. No cross-session pairs, 2048-bin selector fingerprints or historical hashed summaries are mixed into these values. Counts do not establish useful scaffold diversity, and the late rise is descriptive of adaptive sampling. All paid receipts join uniquely to accepted chronology and logged actual origin. Full Child initial/current/preceding origin counts are 770/1817/1763, versus Parent 770/1894/1686; late counts are 145/1008/1022 versus 145/1037/993. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
